conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode; this file mines the List of Terms glossary (pp.11-16) and the Introduction / How to Read / Signs of Strength / Bar Counting Basics sections (pp.17-29)

candidates.name: TrendBar
candidates.quote: trend bar: A bar with a body, which means that the close was above or below the open, indicating that there is at least a minor price movement.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar has a body that is at least a fraction of its range and closed up (long) / down (short).

complexity.reason: single-bar OHLC arithmetic

notes: Same primitive as ranges ch8 R08-01; dedup pass should merge.

candidates.name: DojiBar
candidates.quote: doji: A candle with a small body or no body at all... Neither the bulls nor the bears control the bar. All bars are either trend bars or nontrend bars, and those nontrend bars are called dojis.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar's body is at most a small fraction of its range.

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic

notes: Same primitive as ranges ch8 R08-03.

candidates.name: InsideBar
candidates.quote: inside bar: A bar with a high that is at or below the high of the prior bar and a low that is at or above the low of the prior bar.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar's range is contained within the prior bar's range.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (bar classification; often a breakout-mode setup)

complexity.reason: two-bar comparison

notes: Catalog's InsideBar tests bar N ago against N+1; this is the current-bar-vs-prior form, equivalent at lag 0.

candidates.name: OutsideBar
candidates.quote: outside bar: A bar with a high that is above or at the high of the prior bar and a low that is below the low of the prior bar, or a bar with a low that is below or at the low of the prior bar and a high that is above the high of the prior bar.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar's range engulfs the prior bar's range.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (bar classification; often a breakout-mode setup)

complexity.reason: two-bar comparison

candidates.name: OutsideUpBar
candidates.quote: outside up bar: An outside bar with a close above its open.
candidates.description: An outside bar that closed up (long) / down (short, outside down bar).

complexity.reason: adds a close-vs-open test to OutsideBar

notes: Mirror is OutsideDownBar (R00-06), not a re-derivation of the same candidate.

candidates.name: OutsideDownBar
candidates.quote: outside down bar: An outside bar with a close below its open.
candidates.description: Standalone primitive kept for the book's naming even though it is the mirror of R00-05; some entry bars in a strong bear trend's low 2 setups are explicitly outside down bars.

complexity.reason: adds a close-vs-open test to OutsideBar

candidates.name: DoubleInsideBar_ii
candidates.quote: ii: Consecutive inside bars, where the second is inside the first... it is a breakout mode setup and can become a flag or a reversal setup.
candidates.description: Two consecutive inside bars: bar[0] is inside bar[1], and bar[1] is inside bar[2]. A breakout-mode setup, direction-agnostic (breaks either way).
candidates.pseudocode: high[0] <= high[1] && low[0] >= low[1] && high[1] <= high[2] && low[1] >= low[2]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above / sell stop below the ii's combined range

complexity.reason: fixed two-bar chained inside-bar test

notes: 'Bodies-only ii' variant (tails ignored) noted as less reliable; not separately mechanized here.

candidates.name: TripleInsideBar_iii
candidates.quote: iii: Three inside bars in a row, and a somewhat more reliable pattern than an ii.
candidates.description: Three consecutive inside bars (the ii pattern extended one bar further back).
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above / sell stop below the iii's combined range

complexity.reason: fixed three-bar chained inside-bar test

candidates.name: InsideOutsideInside_ioi
candidates.quote: ioi: Inside-outside-inside—three consecutive bars where the second bar is an outside bar, and the third bar is an inside bar. It is often a breakout mode setup.
candidates.description: Three consecutive bars: bar[1] is an outside bar versus bar[2], and bar[0] is an inside bar versus bar[1].
candidates.pseudocode: high[1] >= high[2] && low[1] <= low[2] && high[0] <= high[1] && low[0] >= low[1]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above / sell stop below the inside bar's range

complexity.reason: fixed three-bar sequence test

candidates.name: OutsideInsideOutside_oio
candidates.quote: oio: Outside-inside-outside, an outside bar followed by an inside bar, followed by an outside bar.
candidates.description: Three consecutive bars: bar[1] is inside bar[2], bar[0] is an outside bar versus bar[1] (both bar[1]-vs-bar[2] and bar[0]-vs-bar[1] are the book's outside/inside tests).
candidates.pseudocode: high[1] <= high[2] && low[1] >= low[2] && high[0] >= high[1] && low[0] <= low[1]

complexity.reason: fixed three-bar sequence test

notes: Brooks does not name an outside/inside reference bar explicitly for the first 'outside' step; read here as outside relative to the bar two back.

candidates.name: OutsideOutside_oo
candidates.quote: oo: Outside-outside, an outside bar followed by a larger outside bar.
candidates.description: Two consecutive outside bars where the second bar's range exceeds the first's.
candidates.pseudocode: high[1] >= high[2] && low[1] <= low[2] && high[0] >= high[1] && low[0] <= low[1] && (high[0] - low[0]) > (high[1] - low[1])
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (bar classification; strong two-sided volatility signal)

complexity.reason: fixed two-bar sequence test

candidates.name: ShavedBody
candidates.quote: shaved body: A candle with no tail at one or both ends. A shaved top has no tail at the top and a shaved bottom has no tail at the bottom.
candidates.description: The bar has (near) zero tail at its top (long side test: close or open equals the high within tolerance) and/or at its bottom.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (bar classification; urgency signal used in sign-of-strength lists)

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic

notes: Shaved bottom is the mirrored test on low[0] vs min(open[0], close[0]); a bar can be shaved at both ends simultaneously.

candidates.name: PauseBar
candidates.quote: pause bar: A bar that does not extend the trend. In a bull trend, a pause bar has a high that is at or below the prior bar, or a small bar with a high that is only a tick or so higher than the previous bar when the previous bar is a strong bull trend bar.
candidates.description: In an up-trend, the current bar's high does not meaningfully exceed the prior bar's high (at/below it, or only a few ticks above a strong prior trend bar). A type of pullback bar.

complexity.reason: two-bar arithmetic

candidates.name: PullbackBar
candidates.quote: pullback bar: A bar that reverses the prior bar by at least one tick. In an uptrend, it is a bar with a low below that of the prior bar.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: in an uptrend, the current bar's low is below the prior bar's low by at least one tick (mirror: high above the prior bar's high in a downtrend).

complexity.reason: two-bar arithmetic

notes: Used as the basic building block for the High 1/2/3/4 and Low 1/2/3/4 leg counters (R00-60/61).

candidates.name: ReversalBarMinimum
candidates.quote: The best-known signal bar is the reversal bar and the minimum that a bull reversal bar should have is either a close above its open (a bull body) or a close above its midpoint.
candidates.description: A candidate bull (bear) reversal signal bar must at least close above its own open, or close above (below) its own midpoint, in a bear (bull) leg.

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic

notes: Gate to be ANDed with the opposite-of-trend-direction context (not itself encoded here).

candidates.name: ReversalBarTailQuality
candidates.quote: A lower tail that is about one-third to one-half the height of the bar and a small or nonexistent upper tail.
candidates.description: Quality filter on a bull reversal signal bar: its lower tail is a substantial fraction of the bar's range and its upper tail is small (mirror for bear reversal bars: upper tail substantial, lower tail small).
candidates.pseudocode: (open[0] - low[0]) >= minTailFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && (high[0] - close[0]) <= maxOppositeTailFraction * (high[0] - low[0])

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic

notes: Brooks gives a range (one-third to one-half); minTailFraction reads the low end.

candidates.name: LowBarOverlapWithPrior
candidates.quote: Not much overlap with the prior bar or bars.
candidates.description: Quality filter: the signal bar overlaps the prior N bars' combined range by at most a fraction F.
candidates.pseudocode: priorRange = highest(high[1], lookback) - lowest(low[1], lookback); overlap = min(high[0], highest(high[1], lookback)) - max(low[0], lowest(low[1], lookback)); overlap <= overlapFraction * priorRange

complexity.reason: small window highest/lowest

candidates.name: Ledge
candidates.quote: ledge: A bull ledge is a small trading range with a bottom created by two or more bars with identical lows; a bear ledge is a small trading range with a top created by two or more bars with identical highs.
candidates.description: Within the last N bars, at least two bars share the same low within a tick tolerance (bull ledge; mirror: same high, bear ledge).
candidates.pseudocode: exists i, j in [0..lookback), i != j: abs(low[i] - low[j]) <= tickTolerance * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (level construction; the ledge low/high is a support/resistance magnet)

complexity.reason: fixed-length window pairwise scan

candidates.name: Barbwire
candidates.quote: barbwire: A trading range of three or more bars that largely overlap and one or more is a doji. It is a type of tight trading range with prominent tails and often relatively large bars.
candidates.description: Over the last N (>=3) bars, the bars largely overlap (a trading range) and at least one is a doji: a choppy, low-edge context that should suppress fresh with-trend or breakout entries.

complexity.reason: depends on a multi-bar trading-range test plus a doji scan

candidates.name: TradingRangeBar
candidates.quote: trading range: The minimum requirement is a single bar with a range that is largely overlapped by the bar before it. It is sideways movement and neither the bulls nor the bears are in control.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar's range overlaps the prior bar's range by at least a fraction F of the prior bar's range.
candidates.pseudocode: overlap = min(high[0], high[1]) - max(low[0], low[1]); overlap >= overlapFraction * (high[1] - low[1])

complexity.reason: two-bar range-overlap arithmetic

notes: This is a proxy for the book's single-bar minimum trading-range test, not the full multi-bar regime concept (see R00-48 AlwaysInDirection for that).

candidates.name: TightTradingRange
candidates.quote: tight trading range: A trading range of two or more bars with lots of overlap in the bars and in which most reversals are too small to trade profitably with stop entries.
candidates.description: Over the last N bars, consecutive bars overlap heavily (a stricter, longer-window version of TradingRangeBar): stand aside from with-trend stop entries.
candidates.pseudocode: for i in 0..lookback-2: (min(high[i], high[i+1]) - max(low[i], low[i+1])) >= tightOverlapFraction * (high[i+1] - low[i+1])

complexity.reason: fixed-length loop of two-bar comparisons

candidates.name: OpeningGap
candidates.quote: An opening gap is a common occurrence and is present if the open of the first bar of today is beyond the high or low of the prior bar (the last bar of yesterday) or of the entire day.
candidates.description: The first bar of the session opens beyond the prior day's extreme (above yesterday's high for an up gap, below yesterday's low for a down gap).
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (chart feature; trade with or fade the gap per other setups)

complexity.reason: needs session boundary detection and the prior session's extreme

candidates.name: MovingAverageGapBar
candidates.quote: moving average gap bar (gap bar): A bar that does not touch the moving average. The space between the bar and the moving average is the gap.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar's low is above the EMA (long) / high is below the EMA (short) -- the bar does not touch the 20-bar EMA.

complexity.reason: needs an EMA

notes: The first MA gap bar in a strong trend's pullback is a described buy/sell setup for a test of the trend extreme (R00-53 second-setup variant).

candidates.name: TwentyMovingAverageGapBars
candidates.quote: 20 moving average gap bars: Twenty or more consecutive bars that have not touched the moving average. Once the market finally touches the moving average, it usually creates a setup for a test of the trend's extreme.
candidates.description: At least N consecutive bars have all been moving-average gap bars in the same direction -- a strong-trend context filter; once the streak ends (a bar finally touches the EMA), a test of the trend extreme is expected.

complexity.reason: fixed-length loop of an EMA-relative test

candidates.name: GapReversal
candidates.quote: gap reversal: A formation in which the current bar extends one tick beyond the prior bar back into the gap. For example, if there is a gap up open and the second bar of the day trades one tick below the low of the first bar, this is a gap reversal.
candidates.description: After an opening gap up, a subsequent bar trades at least one tick below the low of the first bar of the session (mirror: gap down, trades above the first bar's high).
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (chart feature; often a fade setup)

complexity.reason: needs the session's first bar remembered across subsequent bars

candidates.name: MicroMeasuringGap
candidates.quote: micro measuring gap: When the bar before and the bar after a strong trend bar do not overlap, this is a sign of strength and often leads to a measured move.
candidates.description: For a strong bull trend bar at index b, the bar after it (b-1) does not overlap the bar before it (b+1): low[b-1] is at or above high[b+1]. A sign-of-strength primitive distinct from ch8's breakout-gap construction (no breakout requirement here).
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (level construction; often becomes a measuring-gap target midpoint)

complexity.reason: three-bar OHLC comparison

notes: Distinct from ranges ch8 R08-08/R08-09 which require a breakout context first; this is the bare gap definition.

candidates.name: SwingHigh
candidates.quote: swing high: A bar that looks like a spike up on the chart and extends up beyond the neighboring bars. Its high is at or above that of the bar before it and that of the bar after it.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a confirmed swing high pivot, verified one bar after it forms (its high is at or above both neighbors).

complexity.reason: needs the confirming bar to identify the pivot, i.e. lookahead-safe pivot detection

notes: The book allows any number of bars on each side; this is the minimal 1-bar-each-side definition.

candidates.name: SwingLow
candidates.quote: swing low: A bar that looks like a spike down on the chart and extends down beyond the neighboring bars. Its low is at or below that of the bar before it and that of the bar after it.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: mirror of SwingHigh, confirmed one bar after it forms.

complexity.reason: needs the confirming bar to identify the pivot

candidates.name: SwingExtremeExceedsPrior
candidates.quote: higher high: A swing high that is higher than a previous swing high. ... lower low: A swing low that is lower than a previous swing low.
candidates.description: The most recently confirmed swing high is higher than the one before it (bull structure); mirror: most recent swing low is lower than the one before it (bear structure).

complexity.reason: needs the last two confirmed swing pivots retained across bars

candidates.name: SwingRetracementHoldsTrend
candidates.quote: higher low: A swing low that is higher than a previous swing low. ... lower high: A swing high that is lower than a previous swing high.
candidates.description: The most recently confirmed swing low is higher than the one before it (bull trend intact); mirror: most recent swing high is lower than the one before it (bear trend intact).

complexity.reason: needs the last two confirmed swing pivots retained across bars

candidates.name: DoubleTop
candidates.quote: double top: A chart formation in which the high of the current bar is about the same as the high of a prior swing high. That prior high can be just one bar earlier or 20 or more bars earlier.
candidates.description: The current bar's high is within a tick tolerance of a prior swing high within the lookback window (mirror: DoubleBottom on lows).
candidates.pseudocode: exists i in [1..lookback]: SwingHigh[i] && abs(high[0] - high[i]) <= tickTolerance * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop below the double-top bar/signal bar

complexity.reason: needs remembered swing highs plus a tolerance-matching scan

notes: When it forms as a pullback in a bear trend it is called a double top bear flag; not split into a separate candidate.

candidates.name: DoubleBottom
candidates.quote: double bottom: A chart formation in which the low of the current bar is about the same as the low of a prior swing low... it commonly forms in bull flags (a double bottom bull flag).
candidates.description: Mirror of DoubleTop on swing lows.
candidates.pseudocode: exists i in [1..lookback]: SwingLow[i] && abs(low[0] - low[i]) <= tickTolerance * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the double-bottom bar/signal bar

complexity.reason: needs remembered swing lows plus a tolerance-matching scan

candidates.name: TrendingClosesConsecutive
candidates.quote: trending closes: Three or more bars where the closes are trending. In a bull trend, each close is above the prior close, and in a bear trend, each close is lower.
candidates.description: Each of the last N bars closed above (long) / below (short) the prior bar's close -- a strength/context filter (also stated for highs and lows, 'trending highs or lows').

complexity.reason: fixed-length loop over closes

notes: Brooks allows 'one or two bars where the closes are not trending' on long streaks; not modeled here (kept as the strict form).

candidates.name: TrendingSwings
candidates.quote: trending swings: Three or more swings where the swing highs and lows are both higher than the prior swing highs and lows (trending bull swings), or both lower (trending bear swings).
candidates.description: Over the last M confirmed swings, each swing high is higher than the one before it AND each swing low is higher than the one before it (bull); mirror for bear.
candidates.pseudocode: for k in 0..swingsRequired-2: swingHigh(k) > swingHigh(k+1) && swingLow(k) > swingLow(k+1)

complexity.reason: needs a persisted history of confirmed swing pivots, not just the last two

candidates.name: BreakoutBeyondSwingPoint
candidates.quote: breakout: The high or low of the current bar extends beyond some prior price of significance such as a swing high or low, the high or low of any prior bar, a trend line, or a trend channel.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar's high (low) closes/extends beyond the most recent confirmed swing high (low).
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the swing high

complexity.reason: needs the remembered last confirmed swing pivot

notes: The trend-line/channel forms of 'breakout' are covered separately by R00-39/44/45 family (hard complexity, need line projection).

candidates.name: BreakoutPullbackWindow
candidates.quote: breakout pullback: A small pullback of one to about five bars that occurs within a few bars after a breakout... you are expecting the breakout to resume.
candidates.description: Context filter: the market is within N bars of a breakout and has pulled back (a PullbackBar has occurred) without yet resuming -- flags the setup as a breakout-pullback continuation rather than a failed breakout.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context classification enabling a with-trend continuation entry)

complexity.reason: needs the breakout event's bar index retained

candidates.name: BreakoutTestNearEntry
candidates.quote: breakout test: A breakout pullback that comes close to the original entry price to test a breakeven stop. It may overshoot it or undershoot it by a few ticks... or even 20 or more bars later.
candidates.description: Context filter: since the breakout, price has come back within a tick tolerance of the breakout entry price (a test of the breakeven stop), with no bar-count limit.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] <= breakoutEntryPrice + testToleranceTicks * tickSize && low[0] >= breakoutEntryPrice - testToleranceTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (risk-management context; often where a breakeven stop is placed or hit)

complexity.reason: needs the remembered breakout entry price with unbounded lookback

candidates.name: FailedFailureResumes
candidates.quote: failed failure: A failure that fails, resuming in the direction of the original breakout, and therefore a breakout pullback... If the market then trades above the high of a prior bar within the next few bars, the failed breakout has failed and now the breakout is resuming.
candidates.description: After a breakout failed (price traded back through the breakout point), the market now trades back above a recent prior bar's high within a few bars, resuming the original breakout direction -- a second, more reliable with-trend signal.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the resumption bar

complexity.reason: needs both a breakout event and a subsequent failure event tracked, then a resumption test

candidates.name: MicroTrendLineBreakout
candidates.quote: micro trend line breakout: A trend line on any time frame that is drawn across from two to about 10 bars where most of the bars touch or are close to the trend line, and then one of the bars has a false breakout through the trend line... sets up a with-trend entry.
candidates.description: A short trend line fit through 2-10 recent bars is briefly broken by one bar and then price returns to the trend-line side, setting up a with-trend entry (or, if it fails within a bar or two, a countertrend trade).
candidates.pseudocode: microTrendLine = fitLine(pivotSource, microLineBars); low[1] < microTrendLine[1] && close[0] > microTrendLine[0]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the false-breakout bar's high

complexity.reason: needs a fitted trend line over a short variable-length window

candidates.name: ShrinkingStairsMomentumWaning
candidates.quote: shrinking stairs: A stairs pattern where the most recent breakout is smaller than the previous one... a series of three or more trending highs... where each breakout to a new extreme is by fewer ticks than the prior breakout, indicating waning momentum.
candidates.description: Filter: over the last N breakouts to a new trend extreme, each breakout's size (new extreme minus prior extreme) is smaller than the one before it -- momentum is waning, so treat with-trend continuation entries with more caution / favor countertrend.

complexity.reason: needs a persisted history of breakout sizes, itself derived from swing/extreme tracking

candidates.name: NTickFailedBreakout
candidates.quote: five-tick failure: A trade in the Emini that reaches five ticks beyond the signal bar and then reverses. For example, a breakout of a bull flag runs five ticks, and once the bar closes, the next bar has a low that is lower.
candidates.description: A with-trend entry that reached only N ticks beyond the signal bar's trigger before the next bar's low fell back below the signal bar's low (long side) -- a failed scalp, often itself a setup for the opposite side.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (post-hoc classification of a scalper failure, itself a trigger for a reversal trade)

complexity.reason: needs open-position peak profit and the remembered signal-bar low

notes: The 'five ticks' and 'four-tick scalper target needing a six-tick move' figures are Emini-specific; failureTicks is the generalized parameter.

candidates.name: ThreePushWedge
candidates.quote: wedge: Traditionally, a three-push move with each push extending further and the trend line and trend channel line at least minimally convergent, creating a rising or descending triangle with a wedge shape.
candidates.description: Three consecutive swing highs (or lows), each extending further than the last, with the connecting trend line and trend channel line converging -- a reversal or pullback (flag) setup.
candidates.pseudocode: swingHigh(0) > swingHigh(1) > swingHigh(2) && trendLineSlope() and channelLineSlope() converge within lookback
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop below the third push's signal bar (reversal) or buy stop above it (with-trend wedge flag)

complexity.reason: needs pivot detection, line projection, and a convergence test

notes: Any three-push pattern is said to trade like a wedge even without true convergence; the shape requirement is the book's ideal, not a strict gate.

candidates.name: MicroTrendChannelLine
candidates.quote: micro trend channel line: A trend channel line drawn across the highs or lows of three to five consecutive bars.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a short channel line fit through the highs (bear) or lows (bull) of the last 3-5 consecutive bars.

complexity.reason: line projection over a short window

candidates.name: TrendChannelLineOvershoot
candidates.quote: trend channel line overshoot: One or more bars penetrating a trend channel line.
candidates.description: The current bar's high (bull channel line) trades beyond the projected trend channel line -- a climax-warning signal, often preceding a reversal.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (climax context; often the trigger to take profits or fade)

complexity.reason: depends on the channel-line primitive

candidates.name: TrendChannelLineUndershoot
candidates.quote: trend channel line undershoot: A bar approaches a trend channel line but the market reverses away from the line without reaching or penetrating it.
candidates.description: The current bar approaches the projected trend channel line within a tolerance but reverses without reaching it -- a sign of weakening momentum inside the channel.
candidates.pseudocode: high[0] < microChannelLine[0] - undershootTicks * tickSize && high[0] > microChannelLine[0] - undershootBandTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: depends on the channel-line primitive

candidates.name: MicroChannel
candidates.quote: micro channel: A very tight channel where most of the bars have their highs and lows touching the trend line and, often, also the trend channel line... it has no pullbacks or only one or two small pullbacks.
candidates.description: Filter: over the last N bars, most bars touch (within tolerance) both the micro trend line and the micro trend channel line, and at most K PullbackBars occurred -- the most extreme, least-fadeable trend context.

complexity.reason: depends on the channel-line primitive plus a touch-fraction and pullback count

candidates.name: TrendFromOpen
candidates.quote: trend from the open: A trend that begins at the first or one of the first bars of the day and extends for many bars without a pullback, and the start of the trend remains as one of the extremes of the day for much if not all of the day.
candidates.description: Filter/context: the session's directional extreme was set within the first few bars and has not been challenged for most of the session -- a strong with-trend-only day.
candidates.pseudocode: sessionOpenExtremeBarIndex() <= earlyBarsWindow && barsSinceSessionOpenExtreme() >= minPersistBars && sessionExtreme() == sessionOpenExtremeValue()

complexity.reason: needs session-open bookkeeping and a running check that the extreme is unbroken

candidates.name: AlwaysInDirection
candidates.quote: always in: If you have to be in the market at all times, either long or short, this is whatever your current position is... With trend: In general, the direction of the most recent 5 minute chart signal should be assumed to be the trend's direction. Also, if most of the past 10 or 20 bars are above the moving average, trend setups and trades are likely on the buy side.
candidates.description: Global regime concept gating every entry: the market's presumed always-in direction, read here as a proxy -- bullish when most of the last N bars closed above the EMA, else bearish. A design decision is needed before this can be coded exactly as Brooks means it (the most recent significant signal's direction).
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (global context filter used to permit/deny with-trend vs countertrend entries)

complexity.reason: Brooks defines always-in by trader judgment of the 'most recent signal'; the bar-count-above-EMA proxy is one of several possible codings and needs a design decision

notes: MINING.md cites this exact concept as the canonical research-grade example.

candidates.name: BuyClimaxAfterConsecutiveTrendBars
candidates.quote: I saw 15 consecutive bull trend bars on the daily chart after a protracted bull run. This was an unusually strong buy climax, and an important statement by the market.
candidates.description: Take (partial or full) profits on a long when the last N bars were all bull trend bars after a protracted prior bull run -- a buy-climax exhaustion signal (mirror: sell climax after N consecutive bear trend bars).
candidates.pseudocode: for i in 0..climaxBars-1: R00-01[i]; then ctx.OpenPositionProfit() > 0

complexity.reason: fixed-length loop plus open profit

notes: Same family as ranges ch8 R08-20 (climaxBars=6 there); dedup pass should merge, keeping both thresholds as notable variants.

candidates.name: DeepPullbackTreatedAsNewTrend
candidates.quote: the odds that a pullback will get back to the prior trend's extreme fall substantially if the pullback retraces 75 percent or more. For a pullback in a bear trend, at that point, a trader is better off thinking of the pullback as a new bull trend rather than a pullback in an old bear trend.
candidates.description: Filter: once a countertrend pullback has retraced at least X% of the prior trend's range (trend start to trend extreme), stop assuming with-trend continuation is likely and instead treat the pullback as a possible new trend in the opposite direction.

complexity.reason: needs the remembered start and extreme of the identified prior trend leg

candidates.name: ReversalRequiresTrendLineBreakThenTest
candidates.quote: The most common successful reversals first break a trend line with strong momentum and then pull back to test the extreme... the bears can best demonstrate that they have regained control by breaking a bull trend line with strong momentum.
candidates.description: Filter: permit a countertrend/reversal entry only if, within the last N bars, price broke the prevailing trend line with a strong (large-bodied) countertrend move, and the market has now returned to test the old trend's extreme.
candidates.pseudocode: exists i in [0..lookback): trendLineBrokenWithMomentum(i) && distanceToTrendExtreme(0) <= testToleranceTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: needs trend-line detection, a momentum test on the break, and a distance-to-extreme test

notes: Same family as ranges ch8 R08-15/R08-26; recorded fresh here because the front matter states it as the book's single most important reversal principle.

candidates.name: SecondSignalPreferredOverFirst
candidates.quote: second entry: The second time within a few bars of the first entry where there is an entry bar based on the same logic as the first entry... second signal: The second time within a few bars of the first signal where there is a setup based on the same logic as the first signal.
candidates.description: Filter: prefer (or require) the second occurrence of a given setup pattern within N bars of its first occurrence over taking the first occurrence -- used pervasively for countertrend/reversal entries.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (meta-filter over any other setup's own order type)

complexity.reason: 'based on the same logic' requires deciding how setup identity is tracked across occurrences; the once-per-setup-id proxy is one design choice

candidates.name: SecondMovingAverageGapBarSetup
candidates.quote: second moving average gap bar setup: If there is a first moving average gap bar and a reversal toward the moving average does not reach the moving average, and instead the move away from the moving average continues, it is the next reversal in the direction of the moving average gap.
candidates.description: After a first MovingAverageGapBar, if the subsequent pullback toward the EMA fails to reach it and price resumes away from the EMA, the next reversal back toward the EMA is the qualifying (second) setup.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context classification enabling the qualifying reversal entry)

complexity.reason: needs the first gap-bar event and its subsequent failed-pullback state retained across bars

candidates.name: TrailStopBelowLastHigherLow
candidates.quote: trailing a stop: As the trade becomes increasingly profitable, traders will often move, or trail, the protective stop... if they are long in a bull trend, every time the market moves to a new high, they might raise the protective stop to just below the most recent higher low.
candidates.description: For an open long, once a new swing high forms, move the protective stop up to just below the most recently confirmed higher swing low (mirror for shorts: below the most recent lower swing high).
candidates.pseudocode: SwingHigh[1] && lastSwingLow() > priorSwingLow(); stopPrice = lastSwingLow() - stopBufferTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: protective stop order, trailed on each new confirmed higher low

complexity.reason: needs the last two confirmed swing pivots plus position state

notes: Not the same as the catalog's dollar-based TrailingStop; this trails to a structural swing level.

candidates.name: NoPullbackStreakTrendStrength
candidates.quote: There are small, infrequent, and mostly sideways pullbacks. For example, if the Emini's average range is 12 points, the pullbacks will all likely be less than three or four points, and the market will often go for five or more bars without a pullback.
candidates.description: Filter: no PullbackBar has occurred in the last N bars -- a strong-trend confirmation used to favor with-trend entries and disfavor countertrend attempts.

complexity.reason: fixed-length loop over the pullback-bar primitive

candidates.name: NoConsecutiveClosesOppositeEma
candidates.quote: No two consecutive trend bar closes occur on the opposite side of the moving average.
candidates.description: Filter: over the last N bars, no two consecutive trend-bar closes fell on the opposite side of the EMA from the prevailing trend -- a strong-trend confirmation (bull: no two consecutive closes both below the EMA).
candidates.pseudocode: for i in 0..lookback-2: !(R00-01[i] && close[i] < ema(emaLength)[i] && R00-01[i+1] && close[i+1] < ema(emaLength)[i+1])

complexity.reason: fixed-length loop combining the trend-bar primitive with an EMA

candidates.name: VolumeSpikeBreakoutConfirmation
candidates.quote: If the volume of the large breakout bar is 10 to 20 times the average volume of recent bars, the chance of follow-through buying and a possible measured move increases.
candidates.description: Filter: the breakout bar's volume is at least K times the average volume of the recent N bars -- raises confidence in with-trend follow-through.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (confirmation filter, not itself an order)

complexity.reason: a volume average window

candidates.name: FirstPullbackDelayedBars
candidates.quote: The first pullback occurs only after three or more bars of breaking out.
candidates.description: Filter: the first PullbackBar after a breakout does not occur until at least N bars after the breakout -- a sign-of-strength condition for the breakout's quality.

complexity.reason: needs the breakout event's bar index retained

candidates.name: FirstPullbackShortAndShallow
candidates.quote: The first pullback lasts only one or two bars, and it follows a bar that is not a strong bear reversal bar... The first pullback does not reach the breakout point and does not hit a breakeven stop (the entry price).
candidates.description: Filter: the pullback following a breakout lasts at most N bars and its worst excursion does not reach back to the breakout point -- a further sign-of-strength condition.

complexity.reason: needs the pullback's start/duration and the remembered breakout point

candidates.name: PullbackLegCounter
candidates.quote: In a sideways or downward move in a bull trend or a trading range, the first bar whose high is above the high of the prior bar is a high 1, and this ends the first leg... If the market does not turn into a bull swing and instead continues sideways or down, label the next occurrence... as a high 2.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: while a pullback (sideways/down move in a bull trend) is in progress, count each bar whose high exceeds the prior bar's high as ending one leg of the pullback; the running count is the current leg number (high-1, high-2, ...). Resets when the pullback ends (a swing back to a new trend extreme) or the trend context changes. Mirror: low-N counts bars whose low is below the prior bar's low during a bear-trend/range pullback.
candidates.pseudocode: legCount = 0; for each bar since pullback start: if high[bar] > high[bar+1]: legCount += 1 (only the first such bar per leg counts, i.e. the counter does not increment again until the pullback resumes making lower highs)

complexity.reason: a persistent cross-bar counter with reset logic tied to identifying when a pullback starts and ends

notes: This is the core of Brooks's H1/H2/H3/H4 and L1/L2/L3/L4 bar-counting system, arguably the single most load-bearing primitive in the whole trilogy.

candidates.name: PullbackLegNEntry
candidates.quote: If the bull pullback ends after a third leg, the buy setup is a high 3 and is usually a type of wedge bull flag... Some bull pullbacks can grow further and form a high 4.
candidates.description: Enter long when the pullback leg counter reaches exactly N and the current bar's high breaks above the prior bar's high (the High-N signal bar); mirror: enter short on the Low-N signal in a bear trend. legNumber = 1..4 selects High1/2/3/4 (long) or Low1/2/3/4 (short).
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the signal bar's high

complexity.reason: depends on the pullback leg counter primitive

notes: High 2 (bull) / Low 2 (bear) are also called ABC corrections (A = first leg, B = the high1/low1 turn, C = the final leg); not modeled as a separate candidate.

candidates.name: PullbackLegNFailureShiftsControl
candidates.quote: If the low 4 fails (a bar extends above the high of the low 4 signal bar after the low 4 short is triggered), the price action indicates that the bears have lost control... the bears can best demonstrate that they have regained control by breaking a bull trend line with strong momentum.
candidates.description: Context signal: if a triggered Low-N short (typically N=4) is stopped out (a later bar's high exceeds the signal bar's high), treat it as evidence the prevailing bear trend may be losing control -- wait for more price action rather than assuming the bear trend continues (mirror for a failed High-N long).
candidates.pseudocode: PullbackLegNEntry triggered at leg N && high[0] > high[signalBar]
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context signal; the stop-out itself uses the normal signal-bar protective stop)

complexity.reason: Brooks treats this as a judgment call about control shifting, not a fixed rule for what to do next

rejected.quote: Financial news stations do not exist to provide public service... Never watch the news during the trading day.
rejected.reason: news/media commentary; data the engine cannot have and no bar-level test

rejected.quote: The market gravitates toward uncertainty. During most of the day, every market has a directional probability of 50-50... whenever you are uncertain, assume that the market is in a trading range.

chapter_summary: This file mines the book's front matter: the List of Terms glossary (pp.11-16) and the full Introduction plus its How to Read These Books, Signs of Strength, and Bar Counting Basics subsections (pp.17-29). The glossary yielded the trilogy's foundational bar-classification primitives (trend bar, doji, inside/outside bars and their ii/iii/ioi/oio/oo combinations, shaved body, pause/pullback/reversal bars, ledges, barbwire, trading ranges) and structural primitives (swing high/low, higher/lower highs and lows, double tops/bottoms, gaps of several kinds, trend/channel lines). The Introduction contributed a small number of genuinely mechanical context filters (buy-climax after N consecutive trend bars, a 75%-retracement rule for reclassifying a pullback as a new trend, the trend-line-break-then-test reversal principle) among a great deal of psychology/market-structure narrative that was excluded outright (news, institutions, gambling, martingale) rather than forced into 'rejected' one term at a time. The Signs of Strength lists are the densest mechanical material: dozens of bulleted trend/breakout/reversal-bar quality characteristics, most captured here as small filter primitives (volume spike, no-pullback streaks, no straddling the EMA, delayed/shallow first pullbacks) since Brooks presents them as a checklist rather than a single rule. Bar Counting Basics (High 1/2/3/4, Low 1/2/3/4) produced the pullback-leg-counter primitive (R00-60) and its parameterized entry (R00-61), which the dedup/authoring pass should treat as central since every other chapter's pullback-count setups will likely depend on it. Many purely definitional glossary terms with no testable bar-level content (tick, pip, lot, scalp, trader's equation, risk, reward, HFT, institution, fractal, nesting) were read but produced no candidate, by design, per MINING.md's reject criteria.
